The challenged edge claims discourse depends on register. This is a coherent object-level claim: discourse is communication in context, and register is the linguistic mechanism by which context is encoded in language variety selection. Every act of discourse involves choosing a register — without this dimension, discourse cannot signal context and ceases to operate as discourse. The removal test passes: remove register (the variety-selection mechanism) and discourse loses its capacity to contextualize. This is not a meta-level claim about language needing language (Law 2b); it is about how discourse operates as a communicative practice.

The note pins 'chronology (the ordered sequence of temporal events)' — but the chronology entry's accepted definition is a constructed ORDERING DISCIPLINE: units of reckoning, epoch/zero-point, calendrical grid, and crosswalk tables reconciling multiple reckonings. The pinned sense is not the entry's sense (Law 11d). Run the removal test at the entry's actual sense: strip calendrical reckoning systems — calendars, era systems, conversion tables — and historical linguistics does not stop operating. It works in RELATIVE time: the comparative method orders linguistic states (older/newer), reconstructs proto-forms, and establishes regular sound change without any reckoning unit, epoch, or grid. Its real dependence is on the passage of time, which is natural territory outside this kingdom, and a generic appeal to an omnipresent medium files nothing (Law 2b's spirit). Its accepted first leg historical-linguistics DEPENDS_ON language already captures its subject matter; this edge reaches for a construct the discipline does not actually run on.

Constitutive-component dependency, specific and correctly directed. The language entry's own accepted definition names it 'the human-made system of SYMBOLIC SIGNS — vocal, gestural, or written — structured for encoding, transmitting, and decoding meaning.' The sign/symbol function is not an accessory but the constitutive material of the system: strip the sign — the representation that stands for something beyond itself by collective agreement — and there is a system of nothing; the encode/transmit/decode parameters all presume sign-structure. This is the same accepted shape as component dependencies elsewhere on the board (cf. phrase DEPENDS_ON syntax, language DEPENDS_ON logic's accepted neighborhood, writing DEPENDS_ON symbol). The direction is right, not circular: symbol is the more general construct (traffic signs, mathematical and musical notation all stand without language) and already stands accepted with its own dependencies (symbol DEPENDS_ON semiosis). This is not the Law 2b trap — it is not 'language as a concept needs symbols to be thought about' but 'language operates AS a system of symbols.'

The removal test fails at the entry's pinned sense. The phase-locked-vocoder definition carves an STFT-based algorithm whose parameters include analysis/synthesis window LENGTH and hop size — window length, not window SHAPE. The Hann taper (w(n)=0.5*(1-cos(2πn/(N-1)))) is one window function among many: the same algorithm runs on rectangular, Hamming, or Blackman-Harris windows, and removing the Hann window specifically changes nothing about whether the phase-locked vocoder operates — it re-tapers. The real dependency, if any, is on the window function in general or on the STFT itself, and the STFT leg is ALREADY ACCEPTED on this entry (phase-locked-vocoder DEPENDS_ON short-time-fourier-transform stands). Filing the specific-implementation leg is a leap past the general construct: dependency must hold of the target as defined, and the target as defined is one shape in a family of interchangeable tapers. Law 8 removal test fails.

payload.scope: The system of language varieties that a speech community develops for different communicative situations — colloquial, formal, technical, ceremonial, professional — mapped along the dimensions of field, tenor, and mode. This is the LINGUISTIC sense of the word: styles of the language itself. It is distinct from the institutional sense held by the existing 'register' entry (a formal, systematically maintained official list), which is a different construct despite the shared word.
